title: Chat Is Not a Catalog: Why RAG Search Lost to Plain Filters
summary: Anthropic's Claude Duet shows where a big lab draws the approval line for an always-on agent, Symantec catches an attack agent running on hijacked open LLM servers, a 9,000-firm survey puts AI's productivity effect at 0.2% a year, and Recursive's Flint brings a fast open-weights coding model. In the deep dive, a pre-registered experiment shows why a pure chat box makes people search worse than plain filters, and how to design RAG interfaces that keep the corpus visible.
shownotes:
Claude Duet: Anthropic's always-on agent and its three-tier approval model (do it, ask first, never)
"Skynet mode": Symantec honeypot catches an attack agent running on hijacked, unprotected LLM servers
Firm Data on AI (NBER w34836): 78% of firms use AI, 0.2% a year in productivity so far; Gartner CIO survey
Recursive Flint: 40B-total, 2.5B-active open-weights coding model, built largely by an automated research loop
Deep dive: Allu & Kagan's pre-registered experiment where RAG chat search lost to filters, the echo chamber and prompting fatigue mechanisms, and design fixes (hybrid UI, self-querying with editable filters, intent routing, outcome metrics)
